openQuestions.question: Should Gubrud 1997 hold the 'AGI' headline while its wording is read only from the Foresight Archives' current copy, with no capture checked?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes, provisionally: the copy is the organiser's archive of the 1997 conference, the abstract page ties it to that conference, and Goertzel's 2011 account independently reports a 1997 use. Before admission, look up a 1997–1998 capture of www.foresight.org/Conferences/MNT05/Papers/Gubrud/index.html (the cross-family checker may reach the Archive) and record it as the attested date.

openQuestions.question: Is a full-text search before 1997 (Google Books, the Internet Archive's texts, Usenet) needed before calling Gubrud the earliest located?
openQuestions.recommended: Run it in the cross-family check if any of those services answers; until then the search block states that body texts before 1997 were not searched, and the headline is 'earliest located' only.

openQuestions.question: Which publication year should the Goertzel–Pennachin volume carry: 2007 (publisher metadata) or 2005 (Goertzel's post, and one of Legg and Hutter's references)?
openQuestions.recommended: Carry 2007 as the publication date and keep 2005 as a claimed date with both sources side by side; do not resolve until the book's imprint page is read.

openQuestions.question: Should the 1990 Computer Bulletin item 'Clive Sinclair: towards the superintelligent machine' be read before admission, since its adjective form predates Vinge's noun?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes if a copy can be reached; it does not change the 'superintelligence' headline (the criterion takes the noun), but it belongs in the term's search note as the earliest machine-sense adjective found by index.

openQuestions.question: Does the Legg–Hutter definition of intelligence belong under th-term-agi?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep it only if the maintainer wants the term's page to carry the persons' own definitional work; otherwise drop th-def-intelligence-legg-hutter-2007, since the paper does not define 'artificial general intelligence'.

openQuestions.question: Should the earliest-located naming for connectionism be the Dartmouth proposal's heading "Neuron Nets" (1955), given that the heading names a research problem and lists earlier workers?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep it, with the qualification as drafted, and give retrieval of Minsky's 1954 dissertation ("Neural Nets and the Brain Model Problem") priority in the cross-family check; if its title page is retrieved, it becomes the earliest located by correction.

openQuestions.question: The earliest located neural-sense use of "deep learning" (Weston et al., ICML 2008) is late and the abstract refers to "existing approaches to deep learning". Should the term section stay open?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep Weston 2008 as earliest located with the stated search, and ask the cross-family checker to search 2000-2008 (Aizenberg et al. 2000; NIPS 2007 workshop; Bengio TR 1312 of 2007; Gomez and Schmidhuber 2005). Any earlier text meeting the criterion becomes a correction.

openQuestions.question: Should works known only from citations (Linnainmaa 1970, Werbos 1974 and 1982, Parker 1985, LeCun 1985, Kelley 1960, Aizenberg et al. 2000) be candidate document records?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes, as undated document stubs that exist only as objects of credits_work, marked not retrieved; no dates or contents are recorded from them.

openQuestions.question: Is credits_work against one of several cited works (LeCun, Bengio and Hinton cite four; Schmidhuber 2014 cites two) acceptable, or should each cited work get its own record?
openQuestions.recommended: Accept one record with the other works named in the statement, to keep the bound; split only if the integrator needs one edge per work.

openQuestions.question: Several sources are course or third-party copies (McCulloch and Pitts 1990 reprint, Rosenblatt 1958, Hochreiter 1997, Bengio 2009, Deng 2009, PDP chapter 8). Are they acceptable expressions?
openQuestions.recommended: Accept them with the version notes as drafted; each is a scan or text of the published pages. Replace with publisher or author copies at admission where these become retrievable.

openQuestions.question: Should the earliest-located role for 'machine learning' rest on Campaigne's March 1959 conference title, read only in index records with the sense inferred from the venue, or on Samuel (July 1959), the earliest text read in full?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep Campaigne as the earliest located (inferred, flagged) and ask the cross-family checker to try the ACM text; if the text cannot be read before admission, admit Campaigne as earliest located with its inference stated, and keep Samuel as a use. If the maintainer prefers a rule that the headline must rest on a text read in full, swap the roles and record the swap as a correction.

openQuestions.question: The same index-title rule decides the evolutionary (Burgin 1973) and support-vector (Cortes and Vapnik 1995) headlines. Is a title read in a publisher-deposited index record enough for an earliest-located headline?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes for admission as a candidate, with derivation inferred where the sense is not self-evident, but mark both families' searches as weak; the evolutionary headline in particular is likely to be displaced by the 1958–1967 texts if a later pass retrieves them.

openQuestions.question: The dataset already has the concept `reinforcement-learning`. Should the family use that ID instead of `th-fam-reinforcement-learning`?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes: map th-fam-reinforcement-learning to the existing `reinforcement-learning` concept at merge or admission, keeping this group's criterion and search note on it.

openQuestions.question: Sutton and Barto say "reinforcement learning" was first used in the engineering literature in the 1960s; Minsky (1961) uses "reinforcement learning device". Contested?
openQuestions.recommended: No: both are recorded as supported statements of what each text says; the book's statement is about the engineering literature and does not directly deny Minsky's use. Leave them side by side.

openQuestions.question: Should Valiant (1984) be under statistical learning, or under a separate learning-theory heading?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep it under th-fam-statistical-learning with the qualification already given; the scope has no separate learning-theory family.

openQuestions.question: Should the person credited by Kowalski (1988) with suggesting the name 'Prolog' ("Roussel's wife, Jacqueline") get a person record?
openQuestions.recommended: No: keep a literal object naming her as printed. She appears only in this attributed statement; a person record adds nothing and she is not otherwise a public actor in the dataset.

openQuestions.question: The discusses records use attributes.technical.kind values beyond 'definition' ('description' for a text's account of its own system, 'assessment' for Lighthill's judgement). Accept these kinds or fold them into 'definition'?
openQuestions.recommended: Accept 'description' and 'assessment' as distinct kinds: calling ELIZA's or Deep Blue's self-description a definition of a family would overstate it.

openQuestions.question: Is Kowalski 1974's 'predicate logic programming' (acknowledgment) and title 'Predicate Logic as Programming Language' close enough to hold earliest-located-term for 'logic programming'?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes, provisionally, with the qualification as written; the cross-family check should try to retrieve Kowalski's November 1973 DCL Memo 70 and the 1972 Jablonna paper, which could displace it.

openQuestions.question: Should the search-and-planning family hold its earliest-located record on GPS (1958/1959, "planning" as a technique) when the 1956 Logic Theory Machine paper was read only on its opening pages?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes, as stated in the search block; ask the cross-family checker to read P-868 in full for "search" and "planning" and to move the role if an earlier use meets the criterion.

openQuestions.question: The ELIZA, A*, STRIPS and Lighthill documents are marked timeline: true; the Sandewall, Malhotra and Mark papers only support naming records and are marked timeline: false. Is that the right split?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes; the timeline should carry systems, reports and papers of documentary standing, not every naming text.

openQuestions.question: Should th-term-large-language-model require the neural (pre-trained) sense? Brants et al. (2007) use the phrase for n-gram models.
openQuestions.recommended: Keep the scale-based criterion with Brants et al. 2007 as earliest located, and show Witteveen and Andrews (2019) as the earliest located neural-sense use in the note. If the maintainer prefers the neural sense, move earliest-located-term to th-term-llm-witteveen-2019, mark Brants as other-sense and add a correction entry; a fuller neural-sense search (2017-2019 arXiv full texts) would then be needed.

openQuestions.question: Should the Zhao et al. "the research community coins the term" statement be recorded as credits_work to individual cited works?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep the two credits_work records with their qualifications (they credit the community, citing examples), or collapse them into the uses_term record if the integrator finds credits to cited examples misleading.

openQuestions.question: Is the Jeffrey Dean of Brants et al. (2007, Google) the dataset person jeff-dean?
openQuestions.recommended: Do not add an authored record without a source linking the two; the pack records the name as printed.

openQuestions.question: Is "the Transformer" naming record (family) acceptable without an index search for earlier uses of the architecture name?
openQuestions.recommended: Accept with the gap stated in the search block; the cross-family check can probe it.
